To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of the value‐based approach in selection of nursing students has a positive effect on their performance during their first year of nursing education.
the most important factors in selecting students for nursing are: a) academic ability, b) motivation and c) values.
the use of the VBS in the selection of applicants to the undergraduate nursing program was a valid and reliable tool.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying the characteristics of applicants that predict success in a nursing programme.
identifying the most effective ways to select applicants suitable for a career in nursing, and to understand the value of different approaches to selection.
the identification of applicants who are likely to succeed in their chosen nursing career and who are likely to contribute to the profession.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the selection process of the nursing program is not a perfect one.
the selection process of nursing candidates should be based on the values of the profession.
a value based approach to selection of nursing students is a better approach than a purely academic based approach.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an approach to the selection of students into nursing that is based upon a set of values and that we have shown that it works.
we have identified and described the most important factors for the selection of applicants for nursing education.
the selection process should be based on the values that are important in nursing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the value of a college degree is a lot more complicated than the average wage of college graduates.
the value of the nursing profession can be used to identify applicants suitable to a nursing career.
the selection process for nursing should be value-based, rather than solely competency-based.
